consumer:household.spouse_died_2025@i104.question_phrase: Did your spouse die in 2025? (Asked when your filing status is single or head of household.)
consumer:household.spouse_died_2025@i104.source_phrase: Your spouse died in 2025 and you didn’t remarry in 2025.
consumer:household.spouse_died_2025@i104.reason: The input supplies the death-year fact, not eligibility to file jointly. household.widowed_2025 combines it with a single/HOH status guard and refuses the owner-selected death-year situation (BUG-0277); it never treats this answer alone as establishing the quoted joint-return rule. The isolated model response conflated that scope screen with a joint-return eligibility predicate.

consumer:person.age65@i1040sr:p1.source_phrase: "You are considered age 65 on the day before your 65th birthday. As a result, if you were born on January 1, 1961, you are considered to be age 65 at the end of 2025."
consumer:person.age65@i1040sr:p1.reason: Both count a person born on January 1, 1961 as 65. The page also treats a person who died in 2025 before reaching 65 as under 65; s3.elderly_ask then has the credit question asked, and the question only refuses on a wish to claim, so no value depends on the difference.

consumer:person.x_other@i5329:p5.question_phrase: a taxable distribution ...; excess contributions ...; a required minimum distribution
consumer:person.x_other@i5329:p5.source_phrase: Line 4 (p. 5), "you must multiply that amount by 25% instead of 10%"
consumer:person.x_other@i5329:p5.reason: Line 4 reads the screen only through its Part refusal; the rate rule on p. 5 uses no word of the question, whose items concern other Parts.

consumer:sa.unsupported@i1040sca:p10.question_phrase: Any casualty or theft loss; a deduction from the Schedule A line 16 list other than gambling losses; a foreign tax or generation-skipping tax deduction; mortgage interest or points not on Form 1098 or subject to the debt or use limits; or the sales-tax election
consumer:sa.unsupported@i1040sca:p10.source_phrase: Line 12, "Enter on line 12 the total value of your contributions of property other than by cash or check"
consumer:sa.unsupported@i1040sca:p10.reason: sa.line12 refuses on this Schedule A-wide screen as it did before the gate; p. 10 defines nothing the screen asks, and its own conditions are screened by sa.charity_limited and the gift refusals.

limit:p575:p35:1499b8a9.reason: The $22,000 per-disaster limit across plans is never reached: retirement.special asks for "a qualified disaster recovery distribution (whatever the code in box 7), or a repayment of one (Form 8915-F)" and refuses the distribution on yes, and scope.other_income asks for "the 2025 part of a qualified disaster recovery distribution you received in 2023 or 2024, or a 2025 repayment of one (Form 8915-F)" and refuses the return on yes.
